Let <MATH_0001> be a locally Noetherian algebraic stack.
Then <MATH_0002> is quasi-sober (Topology, Definition
<REF_0001>).

We have to prove that every
irreducible closed subset <MATH_0001> has a generic point.
Choose an affine scheme <MATH_0002> and a smooth morphism <MATH_0003>
such that <MATH_0004> is nonempty. Since <MATH_0005> is Noetherian,
the closed subset <MATH_0006> has finitely many irreducible components
(Topology, Lemma <REF_0001>).
Say <MATH_0007> is the decomposition into
irreducible components. As <MATH_0008> is open, the image of
<MATH_0009> contains a nonempty open subset of <MATH_0010>.
Since <MATH_0011> is irreducible, this means that <MATH_0012> is dense.
Since <MATH_0013> is irreducible, it follows that <MATH_0014> is dense for some <MATH_0015>.
Then if <MATH_0016> is the generic point we see that
<MATH_0017> is a generic point of <MATH_0018>.
